profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting at a real-estate investment research firm preparing an external quarterly report titled "Housing Policy Transmission Monitor" for institutional clients. The report synthesizes machine-learning-based house price forecasts for the UK, the US, France, and Switzerland using macro-economic factors such as CPI, US 10-year Treasury rates, GDP, and central-bank balance-sheet size, and it needs to move from the research workstream to the client-content workstream before an executive review. The agenda is to align on which model outputs will be handed off, what goes into the four country packs, how the next-4-quarters forecasts will be presented, and what counts as being ready for circulation. The expected outcome is an apparently shared plan for the Thursday handoff, Monday executive review, and the ownership of the shared files.

members.name: Elena Ward
members.expertise: Housing economics, applied machine learning, forecast validation, cross-country macro analysis
members.background: Elena leads the firm's research team that built the kNN and tree-bagging models used in the housing outlook and previously worked in central-bank research covering policy transmission into asset prices.
members.private_state: She wants the external report to preserve enough methodological nuance that clients do not overinterpret the forecasts, and she is worried the content team will strip out caveats and sensitivity context that protect the credibility of the research.
hidden_assumptions: When someone asks for the "latest numbers," they mean the most recent rerun using the newest available macro releases, even if that supersedes a previously circulated deck.
A "country sheet" naturally includes not only headline charts but also the core assumptions, model-selection note, and sensitivity-test summary needed to interpret the forecast.
Once the research team has completed QA, reproduced the outputs, and locked the code notebook, the material is effectively "signed off" for downstream use.
A "next 4 quarters" forecast is a rolling horizon starting from each country's latest observed quarter in the research dataset, not necessarily a publication-calendar grid.
The shared handoff artifact is the research workbook and linked output tables in the analytics SharePoint, which downstream teams will pull from directly.

members.name: Marcus Liu
members.expertise: Cross-functional publication planning, executive decks, compliance routing, content packaging for institutional clients
members.background: Marcus manages the conversion of analyst outputs into client-ready reports and slide packs, coordinating design, legal/compliance, and distribution for multi-market publications.
members.private_state: He needs a stable package that can move through design and compliance without late revisions, and he is concerned about slipping the publication calendar if research keeps refining the numbers.
hidden_assumptions: When someone refers to the "latest numbers," they mean the latest approved figures already in the master deck unless a formal reversioning decision has been announced.
A "country sheet" means a clean one-page client-facing summary per market; methodological backup belongs elsewhere and is not part of the handoff pack.
Material is not truly "signed off" until compliance and brand review are complete, because those are the approvals that govern external circulation.
A "next 4 quarters" table should map to the publication's labeled calendar quarters so every country can sit on the same comparison grid.
The operational handoff should be a static export set in the content library, because design and compliance should not work off live research files.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the latest numbers
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to use the "latest numbers" in the country packs and executive deck.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena means the model outputs rerun with the newest available macro releases, including the recent CPI and central-bank balance-sheet updates that changed some near-term forecasts.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Marcus means the figures already present in the current approved master deck from the January data freeze, unless someone explicitly opens a new version cycle.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both teams routinely say "latest" as shorthand, and because both are thinking of a concrete, recent set of numbers that they personally treat as authoritative, the phrase feels fully specific without prompting clarification.

misalignment_points.topic: What is included in each country sheet
misalignment_points.surface_form: They align on producing four "country sheets" for the UK, US, France, and Switzerland.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena assumes each country sheet includes the headline forecast chart, the macro-driver summary, a short note on whether kNN or tree-bagging was selected, and at least a compact sensitivity-test panel or footnote.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Marcus assumes each country sheet is a one-page client-ready summary with the key chart, a short market takeaway, and no methodological detail beyond a generic source line.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The term "country sheet" sounds operationally settled because both have used it in prior projects, but each function has internal norms about what belongs in such a sheet, so the boundary difference stays invisible.

misalignment_points.topic: When the pack is signed off
misalignment_points.surface_form: They discuss getting the pack "signed off" before Monday's executive review and client circulation planning.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena believes "signed off" means research QA is complete, the outputs are reproducible, and the charts no longer need analytical changes.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Marcus believes "signed off" means the pack has cleared compliance and brand review and is safe to circulate externally or share beyond the immediate project group.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both treat sign-off as a standard milestone and neither expects the other to be using a different approval standard, especially in a coordination meeting focused on timing rather than governance terminology.

misalignment_points.topic: How the next 4 quarters forecast is indexed
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to show the "next 4 quarters" forecast for each country in the summary table.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena means a rolling four-quarter-ahead forecast from the last observed quarter available in each country's input series, which may differ slightly by market because of release timing.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Marcus means four labeled calendar quarters aligned across all four countries in the publication table so readers can compare markets side by side on the same quarter headings.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase "next 4 quarters" normally sounds exact, and both interpretations produce four forecast values, so the mismatch hides inside indexing conventions rather than the visible number of periods.
